Package frc.robot.util

Class Vec2

java.lang.Object
frc.robot.util.Vec2
public class Vec2 extends Object
A 2D vector class for representing and manipulating 2D coordinates and directions.

This immutable class provides common vector operations including addition, subtraction, scalar multiplication, dot product, and magnitude calculations. It's commonly used for representing velocities, positions, and forces in 2D space.

The class is immutable, meaning all operations return new Vec2 instances rather than modifying the original object.

    • dot

      public double dot(Vec2 other)
      Computes the dot product with another vector. The dot product represents the projection of one vector onto another. For perpendicular vectors, the dot product is zero.
      Parameters:
      other - The other vector
      Returns:
      The dot product as a scalar (this · other)

    • norm

      public Vec2 norm()
      Returns the normalized (unit) version of this vector. The normalized vector has a magnitude of 1 but points in the same direction. For zero vectors, returns a zero vector to avoid division by zero.
      Returns:
      A new Vec2 with the same direction but magnitude of 1

    • rotate

      public Vec2 rotate(edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Rotation2d angle)
      Rotates this vector by a given angle, counterclockwise.

      This multiplies the translation vector by a counterclockwise rotation matrix of the given angle. 

       [x_new] = [other.cos, -other.sin][x]
 [y_new] = [other.sin,  other.cos][y]
      Parameters:
      angle - The angle to rotate by
      Returns:
      A new Vec2 representing the rotated vector

    • mag

      public double mag()
      Calculates the magnitude (length) of this vector. Computed as sqrt(x² + y²).
      Returns:
      The magnitude of this vector

    • mag2

      public double mag2()
      Calculates the squared magnitude of this vector. Computed as x² + y². This is more efficient than mag() when you only need to compare magnitudes, since comparing squares preserves the order.
      Returns:
      The squared magnitude of this vector
